```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has sourced evidence that buyers pay for this exact product standalone. dashp, a solo builder, is cited at ~$100k ARR. D2DHQ publishes $149-$499/mo flat pricing plus a $500 setup fee. A second indie builder is publicly pricing at $20-$125/mo. B has no sourced example of anyone paying for file-arrival monitoring as a standalone product. Its paid comparables, Files.com and Nodinite, sell it bundled inside larger platforms.",
    "A's demand evidence is recent and costly to the people affected: a litigated $217,494.60 commission dispute and a rep's complaint about unpaid commissions. B's demand quotes are from 2012 and 2016, and its own Case Against cites Definite saying the fix is 'a cron job and a Slack webhook in an afternoon.' That points to free self-builds rather than paid demand.",
    "A's payer is clearly identified (owner or sales-ops manager), and A has a published price anchor that a new entrant can undercut. B's price ceiling is capped by Files.com, which offers the same 'Expectations' capability within its $199/mo plan, and B's brief lists 'will customers pay standalone?' as an unresolved open question.",
    "A's main risk is the sales cycle, which its own brief puts at ~5 months per closed deal (dashp's account). That threatens the 90-day target, but it is a speed problem against a market with demonstrated willingness to pay. B's main risk is that it may have no standalone market at all, which is the worse failure mode for a first bet.",
    "B's acquisition channel is only generic B2B SaaS CPC benchmarks. Its SEO cost estimate is marked [unsourced], and the brief admits incumbents already rank for the target queries. That leaves no credible sourced path to a first customer in 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is the weakest support in either brief. The StackOverflow quote (2012) describes users being unable to log in to SFTP. That is a server-availability problem, which WatchFor's free and cheap tiers already cover, not the missing or late file problem B proposes to solve. The other forum quote is from 2016. The HN item is a bare seed link with no quoted content. That leaves effectively one decade-old, on-target anecdote, and it shows someone who did not notice the failure, not someone willing to pay to prevent it.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's sourced ~5-month trust-based sales cycle and an ICP of only 'hundreds' of companies could easily push the first paying customer past 90 days. A's crowded field (6+ direct competitors, including an identical solo builder) also weakens differentiation. A wins mainly because B's own brief undermines standalone willingness to pay, while A's brief documents real revenue for this exact product."
}
```
